# ADR-047 — Health storage is daily aggregates plus sessions; intraday is heart-rate only; nothing is auto-deleted

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Health storage is daily aggregates plus sessions; intraday is heart-rate only; nothing is auto-deleted.** Phase 6A stores one `health_daily_metrics` row per `(connection, metric, local_date)`, session rows for `sleep`/`exercise`, and **intraday samples for `heart-rate` alone** — every other metric is acquired at daily or session granularity, which also makes the types that expose **no `list` operation at all** (`total-calories`, `calories-in-heart-rate-zone`, `floors`) first-class rather than special cases. Units are **metric-implied** (the API bakes them into field names), so no unit column exists; per-metric semantics are enforced in Zod against a code catalog, while Postgres enforces shape and identity. **True zero and missing are structurally distinct** — a CHECK makes their collapse impossible — and **no read model, aggregate or brief collector may ever `COALESCE(value, 0)`**. **No health data is ever automatically deleted, expired or pruned.** Any retention policy is a separate, explicitly-approved decision and would ship disabled by default; only operational metadata (`health_sync_runs`, expired OAuth states) is swept (Phase 6 Checkpoint 6.0, user-approved 2026-08-24) **[Present state corrected by ADR-057; the sweep clause is now TRUE in both halves — see ADR-062.]**
